items.statement: The Zygmund conjecture for square-summable f along Lipschitz line fields (195-204), and Stein's singular integral variant (206-207), are stated as open and are not proved.

The proved statement is a lower density bound for indicator functions ('We obtain the following lower density bound for indicator functions', 212-220); it does not give the differentiation formula for general square-summable f.
The proof of Proposition 7.6 (lower.bound) is 'The reader will happily check that ... suits their needs', with δ and c(n) given explicitly (1944-1951).
The proof of Corollary 6.4 (cor.ub) consists only in setting δ = min{δ_{upper.bound}, δ_{Z.1}(n,Λ,1/2)} (1620).
Corollary 5.16 (lb.2) is stated with no proof environment in the source.
Lemma 3.12 (jac.g) has no proof environment; its proof is the prose derivation of 607-665, ending 'In view of (eq.3), we obtain the next lemma' (664).
The two items of 8.3 (8.3.1 at 2076 and 8.3.2 at 2098) are derived in prose (2079-2096, 2105-2123) without proof environments.
Claim #3 inside the proof of 7.3 invokes 'a standard application of homology theory, see, e.g., [DEP.05c, 4.6.1]' when m < n−1 (1715); that step is external to the paper.
The existence of nearly Nikodym sets is attributed to Nikodym (n=2, m=1) and Falconer (m=n−1) with literature references (805-809); no proof is given in the paper.

Other inputs are cited rather than proved: coarea (449-491; Evans–Gariepy, GMT), the Lipschitz retraction (503; GMT 3.1.20), Lipschitz extension (505; GMT 2.10.43), von Neumann selection (867; Srivastava 5.5.3), Lusin (877; GMT 2.5.3), Dynkin class (752; Cohn 1.6.2), coarea on the annuli (2219, 2227; Evans–Gariepy 3.4.3), the polynomial-zero-set fact (1138; GMT 2.6.5).

The Appendix (71 at 2245-2250, 72 at 2256-2261, with proofs 2252-2254 and 2263-2267) is inside a comment environment (2240, 2268) and is not part of the published article; the author calls both results classical (2243) and gives the second proof only 'for the reader familiar with normal currents'.

Unbalanced parenthesis: the argument of H^m opens '(x+W_0(x)' and never closes, so the set expression and the equation are literally malformed in both the English (154) and French (171) abstracts.
